persona.label: Rushed but qualified
persona.description: Busy professional between meetings. Terse, answers several things at once. Should be transferred.
persona.behavior: You are between meetings and have about five minutes. Your first reply says something like "ok but make it fast, I'm busy." Use short, lowercase texts with no pleasantries. When asked something, answer it, and volunteer one or two related facts if it saves time. Round numbers the way people do ("about 520", "owe like 310k"). If the assistant is slow or repetitive, show mild impatience. You want a lower rate and you want to talk to someone today.

transcript.text: Hi Taylor, this is Riley, an automated assistant with Harborline Home Loans, following up on the refinance inquiry you just submitted. Do you have a couple of minutes for a few quick questions? You can reply STOP at any time to opt out.
ok but make it fast, i'm busy. looking to lower my rate, currently at 7.25
Got it, I'll keep this quick. Roughly what's your home worth, and about how much do you still owe on the mortgage? If texting gets to be too much, I can set up a call for a better time instead.

handoff.borrower_summary: Taylor Brooks, primary residence worth ~$520k, owes ~$310k, current rate 7.25%, self-reported credit 740+. Busy, wants to move fast.
objections_raised: Short on time - asked to keep it fast
handoff.recommended_next_step: Call Taylor today; keep it brief and discuss rate-and-term options.

objections.rationale: Agent acknowledged it ("Got it, I'll keep this quick"), offered both paths (quick texts now or "I can set up a call for a better time instead"), and kept the questions tight.

judge.naturalness_rationale: Messages are short, warm, and adapted to a hurried borrower: "Got it, I'll keep this quick," "Last one," and a direct "Yes." There is no filler or repetition.
judge.experience_rationale: The borrower got a fast, respectful exchange and a quick handoff at [6]. However, "Yes" promises a same-day call without hedging, and the agent never said how contact would happen (phone vs. text) or that the loan officer would provide the quote.

compliance_issues.excerpt: Yes. I'm connecting you with a licensed loan officer now.
compliance_issues.explanation: This flatly confirms a call today without knowing loan officer availability, which is mild over-promising on timing.

compliance_issues.excerpt: so you won't need to repeat yourself
compliance_issues.explanation: The loan officer will likely verify details before quoting, so an absolute promise of no repetition may set a false expectation.

judge.handoff_summary_rationale: The summary is accurate and complete, and all fields match the transcript (520k/310k/7.25%/740+/primary/ASAP), so a loan officer could call immediately. However, the open question "What rate/payment could they get?" was never asked by the borrower, which is a minor fabrication.

annotations.note: Clearly identifies itself as "an automated assistant," names the inquiry source, and gives the STOP opt-out up front.
Handles the busy objection with both options: quick questions now or "set up a call for a better time instead."
The agent recognized that the borrower volunteered occupancy and credit, and skipped those questions instead of re-asking.
"Yes." unconditionally promises a call today and doesn't specify the contact method or rough timing.
"you won't need to repeat yourself" overpromises, since the loan officer may need to confirm details before quoting.

judge.overall_notes: This was an efficient, compliant, and natural conversation that respected the borrower's time and produced a strong handoff. The main gaps are unhedged timing promises at handoff and one invented open question in the summary.
